overview: Both are stress- and ageing-associated plant hormones, but they trigger very different physical processes.
genZNote: Ethylene: the ripening and 'let it fall' gas. Abscisic acid: the drought-and-dormancy hormone.

aspects.label: Physical State
aspects.valueA: A gas at room temperature — the only gaseous plant hormone.

aspects.label: Signature Role
aspects.valueA: Promotes fruit ripening, leaf/flower abscission (falling off), and senescence.
aspects.valueB: Promotes seed dormancy and stomatal closure under water stress.

aspects.label: Practical Example
aspects.valueA: Used commercially to ripen fruits after harvest.
aspects.valueB: Levels rise sharply in wilting or drought-stressed plants.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Ethylene is the only plant hormone that is a gas, which is why it can be applied to whole rooms of fruit for artificial ripening.
overlay.memoryTrick: Ethylene = ripens and drops things. Abscisic acid = dormancy and drought defence, despite the misleading 'abscisic' name.
overlay.commonMisconception: Abscisic acid does not actually cause leaf/fruit abscission directly in most modern understanding — that role belongs mainly to ethylene, despite abscisic acid's name.
